_comment: D-1 / D2-01..04. A DIFF over day 1, not a second fixture set — see data/mock/db.ts's applyDay2. Day 1 is the scene the demo opens on; day 2 is that same scene the following morning, after a night in which the EA kept working and the clock kept moving. Everything here is something that changed BECAUSE time passed, which is the only thing a second day is for.

expire._comment: c1's expiry has passed. The card is not merely gone: its then-what was applied, so the recommended option was taken and the history says via expiry. That is the promise the card made in silence, kept while nobody was watching.

laterReturns._comment: c3 was put off until this morning and is back, open, in Needs you — a Later that never returns is a card quietly dropped.

_overnightRun: T-5/WK-04: the EA's redaction run on t2 finished overnight. The MARKER goes (a marker is about now) but the delegation does not: a run ending is not the task finishing, and t2 is still in progress. The run and its usage row are seeded the same way the subtask's are — one cost record (ADR-43).

goalProgress._comment: LG-1, resolution #65 and contract §4.20: the backend advances kpis[].value from agent work and appends the goal's history. Day 2 moves one KPI so the card shows agent-tracked progress rather than a number that only ever changes when Josh types it.

overnightSubtask._comment: t1-3 is the EA's last open subtask on t1; overnight it finished. D2-04 asks for the subtask done, the cost recorded and the EA report present, so the delegation is marked done and t1 gains the report it did not have yesterday.
overnightSubtask._cost: T-4: the cost is no longer a number of its own here. It is `usage.costAud` below, and `applyDay2` reads the delegation's cost off that row — one cost record (ADR-43).
overnightSubtask._fileComment: X-1: the deliverable the overnight run produced. A report used to carry its own {name, ref} pairs; now the file is an Attachment record like every other file, and `advanceToDay2` appends it to db.files.
